- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly in early horizon.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., 73+), leading to overshoots in 30-day forecast; cap or dampen upward momentum after peaks.
- Mean reversion is evident: model often fails to recognize that prices return to prior 10-15 day averages after sharp moves; apply smoothing or decay toward recent mean.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 5-7 days of the 30-day horizon — model tends to overreact to recent sentiment shifts; use lagged sentiment or moving average to anchor early predictions.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with trend direction; align forecast with sentiment momentum rather than absolute price levels.
